summary: Read a Unicode code point at a UTF-16 string index.
documentation: codePointAt reads the code unit at the requested index. At a leading surrogate followed by a trailing surrogate it combines the pair into one code point; at a trailing surrogate it returns that code unit alone. An index outside the string produces undefined.
inputs: An object with text and an integer index measured in UTF-16 code units.
returns: A numeric code point or code-unit value, or null when the index is outside the string.
caution: String indices count UTF-16 code units, not visible characters or grapheme clusters. Do not advance one index per displayed character when iterating emoji text.
scenarios: Inspect an unexpected character in a pasted customer name.
Diagnose an emoji at a known JavaScript string offset.
Show numeric Unicode values in a local text-debugging tool.
title: Inspect a Unicode position
problem: Return text.codePointAt(index), converting only an undefined result to null. Preserve a valid zero value. A trailing-surrogate index must return that code unit rather than the whole emoji.
hint: Use the nullish-coalescing operator to convert undefined to null without replacing zero.
goal: Use String.codePointAt() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
